title: Harvard men's volleyball announces incoming class of 2030
text:
Harvard men’s volleyball announces incoming class of 2030
Harvard Men's Volleyball head coach Brian Baise announced on July 8 the program's incoming Class of 2030, consisting of five athletes set to arrive in Cambridge for the 2026-27 academic year.
The first-year class includes two outside hitters, two setters, and one middle blocker. The outside hitters are Mateo Sanz from Texas and Simon Vardeh from Newton, Massachusetts. The setters are Kahi Marumoto from Hawaii and Tyler Pence from Newport Beach, California. Miles Hiscox will join as a middle blocker from Vancouver, British Columbia.
These new recruits will join a Crimson team expected to return all players from its 2026 roster except for graduating seniors Zach Berty and Brian Thomas. Among the returning players are Owen Woolbert, who earned All-EIVA Second-Team honors in 2026, and Thomas Phung, who received All-EIVA Honorable Mention recognition last season.
Each member of the incoming class brings significant experience and achievements at both club and high school levels. Hiscox played for Apex Volleyball Club and Team Canada at international competitions such as the U19 World Championships in Uzbekistan. Marumoto captained teams at Punahou School in Hawaii and Outrigger Canoe Club while earning several academic awards. Pence led his high school team to league titles in California while serving as captain for both indoor and beach volleyball squads. Sanz represented Chile’s national youth teams at Pan-American Cups while also excelling in basketball and track during his time at The Woodlands High School in Texas. Vardeh was a four-year varsity starter at Newton North High School in Massachusetts with multiple state-level accolades.
The new additions aim to strengthen Harvard's roster as it prepares for future seasons following recent graduations.
